questions.stem: A 60 W bulb and a 100 W bulb designed for 220 V are connected in SERIES across a 220 V supply. Which will be BRIGHTER and why?

options.option_text: The 100 W bulb, because its power rating is higher
The 60 W bulb, because its resistance is higher and more power dissipates in it

questions.explanation: Resistance R = V²/P. 60 W bulb has R = 220²/60 ≈ 807 Ω. 100 W bulb has R = 220²/100 = 484 Ω. In SERIES, same current flows through both; power dissipated P = I²R → the HIGHER-resistance (60 W, the lower-rated) bulb dissipates more power and glows brighter. Counter-intuitive result — classic exam trap.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Consider the following about ELECTRIC POWER in a purely RESISTIVE circuit. 1. P = V²/R. 2. P = I²R. 3. P = V·I. 4. In an AC purely resistive circuit, RMS values are used for V and I in power calculations. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. The three power formulae are equivalent through V = IR. For AC resistive circuits, average power = V_rms × I_rms (with V_rms = V_peak/√2 for sinusoidal). In reactive circuits add the cosφ (power factor).

questions.stem: Three resistors of 4 Ω, 6 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in PARALLEL across a 12 V battery. The total current drawn is:
questions.explanation: 1/R_eq = 1/4 + 1/6 + 1/12 = 3/12 + 2/12 + 1/12 = 6/12 → R_eq = 2 Ω. I = V/R = 12/2 = 6 A. Always compute R_eq first, then I = V/R_eq.

questions.stem: Match the instrument with its PRINCIPLE of operation. A. Electric motor. B. Transformer. C. Electric generator (dynamo). D. Galvanometer. List-II: 1. A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a torque (motor effect). 2. Mutual induction. 3. Electromagnetic induction (moving conductor in magnetic field). 4. Deflection of a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field.
questions.explanation: Motor — motor effect (Fleming's Left-Hand rule). Transformer — mutual induction (Faraday). Generator — electromagnetic induction (Fleming's Right-Hand rule). Galvanometer — torque on coil causes deflection proportional to current. Note 1 vs 4 are subtly different: motor converts to mechanical rotation; galvanometer produces a measured deflection.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): A transformer does not work on DC supply. REASON (R): A steady DC current produces a constant magnetic flux, which does not induce an EMF in the secondary coil.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

questions.explanation: Transformers rely on a CHANGING flux to induce EMF in the secondary (Faraday's law: EMF = -dΦ/dt). Steady DC gives dΦ/dt = 0 → no induction → no stepped voltage. (Modern DC-DC converters exist but they CHOP the DC into pulses first to make dΦ/dt ≠ 0.)
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries a current of 5 A. The magnetic field at 0.1 m from the wire is (μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A):
questions.explanation: B = μ₀ I / (2π r) = (4π × 10⁻⁷ × 5) / (2π × 0.1) = (4 × 10⁻⁷ × 5) / (2 × 0.1) = (20 × 10⁻⁷) / 0.2 = 10⁻⁵ T. Ampere's law for a long straight wire.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT use the principle of ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION?
questions.explanation: Electric iron uses simple JOULE HEATING in a resistive element — not electromagnetic induction. Induction stove (eddy currents in the iron pot), generator (Faraday), transformer (mutual induction) all rely on EMI.

questions.stem: A fuse in an electric circuit is designed to:

options.option_text: Break the circuit when current exceeds a rated limit, protecting devices
Increase the current capacity of the wire

questions.explanation: A fuse is a thin wire of low-melting-point alloy that melts and breaks the circuit when excessive current flows (short circuit, overload). Protects appliances and wiring from damage/fire. Modern alternative: MCB (Miniature Circuit Breaker) — reusable.
